decisions.quote: We successfully replicated the basic congruency effect of the original study, that is, the interaction effect between direction of manual response and time reference when participants perform a sensicality judgment. In contrast to the original study, this congruency effect was not signiﬁcantly modulated by the magnitude of time shift.
decisions.reason: The paper re-tests two predictions from Sell and Kaschak (2011) Experiment 1—the two-way space-time congruency interaction and its three-way modulation by time-shift magnitude—and explicitly contrasts the non-significant modulation with the original study while qualifying its discussion summary ('Although the threefold interaction ... was not significant in our study, our results largely replicate those of Sell and Kaschak'). Under the codebook, a tested finding that the paper itself contrasts with the original ('in contrast to the original study') alongside a replicated effect makes the outcome mixed.

parent_objection: The discussion says: Although the threefold interaction ... was not significant in our study, our results largely replicate those of Sell and Kaschak (2011). Is this a genuine overall verdict under Rule 1, or only a focal-effect assertion? The first reply uses Rule 2 contrasting component results without settling the broad post-contrast verdict. Read abstract and full discussion, not just the three-way p-value. Decide under exact codebook priority: a genuine overall verdict outranks component contrasts; focal-effect confirmation does not. Explain scope of largely replicate rather than assume that partially successful or largely means either category automatically.

blind_target.authors: Sell, A. J. & Kaschak, M. P.
blind_target.title: Processing time shifts affects the execution of motor responses.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The present study is a replication of Sell and Kaschak’s (2011) Experiment 1 (Movement Condition).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Although the threefold interaction between Response location, Time shift direction, and Shift magnitude on RT was not signiﬁcant in our study, our results largely replicate those of Sell and Kaschak (2011).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly give an overall verdict that their results largely replicate the original, acknowledging the nonsignificant three-way interaction in the same sentence. Under rule 1 this overall verdict outweighs the component-level contrast in the abstract.
